main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow roof slope above a vertical plank wall with an arched double door and two lit windows
top_band: At x=55: light snow roof slope (L 200-249, with some 166 and 130 shading) from rows 8 to about 50. It is a big foreshortened roof surface, scalloped and lighter than the wall. A bright snow eave lip closes it at the front, and the dark brown plank wall starts at row 52.
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above, like the tiled roofs on the Beodeul reference houses, and it clearly sits above the vertical plank wall. A bright snow eave band at rows 47-50 marks the front edge. Dark wall tone and icicles directly under it read as eave shadow. The windows have snow sills and dark frames, and the door has an arched inset with iron straps, so the front is not painted flat. The wall (rows 52-76) is a proper south face. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The snow roof has five lightness steps (249, 228, 200, 166, 130) in scalloped tile-like clumps, and the wood wall has several browns with plank grain. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean navy and brown, as in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Density is below the references: 9 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 42 distinct colours against 66 and 185. The piece still has no large flat areas, and the windows, door, wreaths, icicles and snow drifts add detail. A careful artist would likely accept it next to the references, though it is a little thinner.
